title: ClusterIP – The Internal Service 🏠
description: Create a Service that provides stable internal communication between your apps.

slides.title: What is ClusterIP? 🏠
slides.content:
# The default, internal‑only Service type

ClusterIP gives your Service a **virtual IP** that is only reachable **from within the cluster**. No outside traffic can access it directly.

It’s perfect for:
- Backend APIs communicating with each other
- Database connections between microservices
- Any internal traffic that doesn’t need external exposure

slides.title: ClusterIP in YAML 📝
slides.content:
## A minimal ClusterIP Service

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: backend-svc
spec:
  selector:
    app: backend
  ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 80          # Service port
      targetPort: 8080  # Container port
  type: ClusterIP
```

- `port`: the port the Service listens on (other apps use this).
- `targetPort`: the port on the Pod where the application listens.
- If `type` is omitted, it defaults to ClusterIP.

quizData.question: What does the `targetPort` field specify?

options.text: The port on the container where the app listens
The external port for load balancing

quizData.explanation: targetPort is the container port the Service forwards traffic to.

slides.title: How ClusterIP Works 🔄
slides.content:
## kube‑proxy magic

When you create a ClusterIP Service, the kube‑proxy component on every node programs **iptables (or IPVS) rules**. Traffic sent to the Service’s ClusterIP gets intercepted and load‑balanced to a random healthy Pod.

- By default, session affinity is **None** (each request can go to a different Pod).
- You can set `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` to stick a client to a specific Pod (based on client IP).

slides.title: Create and Test a ClusterIP Service
slides.codeSnippet:
kubectl apply -f backend-svc.yaml
kubectl get services
kubectl describe service backend-svc
# From another Pod, access:
curl http://backend-svc

quizData.question: True or False: A ClusterIP Service can be accessed from your laptop outside the cluster.
quizData.explanation: ClusterIP is internal only; you need NodePort, LoadBalancer, or port‑forward to reach it from outside.

slides.title: Multi‑Port Services 🧩
slides.content:
## One Service, many ports

A single Service can expose multiple ports (e.g., HTTP and gRPC). Each port must have a name.

```yaml
ports:
  - name: http
    port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
  - name: grpc
    port: 50051
    targetPort: 50051
```

This is cleaner than creating separate Services for the same set of Pods.

quizData.question: Why might you use a multi‑port Service?

options.text: To expose two different Pod groups
To expose both HTTP and gRPC on the same set of Pods

quizData.explanation: It allows a single logical Service to handle multiple protocols on different ports.
